RPDR.title: A whole pawn up, and it's a draw #shorts
RPDR.desc:
King and rook pawn against a lone king: if the defending king reaches the corner in front of the pawn, it's a draw. Pushing the pawn to the seventh row stalemates Black, and stepping away lets the king walk back to the corner.

Did you know this one?

#chess #chessendgame #stalemate

EPPN.title: En passant looks possible here, but it's illegal #shorts
EPPN.desc:
Black plays c7-c5, right next to White's pawn on b5. Normally bxc6 en passant would be legal, but both pawns would leave the fifth row and the rook on h5 would check the white king on a5. A move that leaves your own king in check is never legal.

Did you see the rook?

#chess #enpassant #chessrules

BRK2.title: Same pawns, but Black moves first. Only one move saves him #shorts
BRK2.desc:
The pawn breakthrough position with Black to move. 1...b6! is the only move that holds: 2.axb6 axb6 3.cxb6 cxb6 and nothing gets through. Any other move lets White break through with b6.

Would you have found b6?

#chess #chessendgame #chesspuzzle

CSM2.title: Castling can be checkmate #shorts
CSM2.desc:
The black king is on g1. The bishop on d5 covers g2 and h1, the knight on g4 covers f2 and h2. 1.O-O-O puts the rook on d1, it checks along the first row, and it's checkmate.

Have you ever mated with castling?

#chess #checkmate #castling

PRKM.title: Make a queen and it's a draw. Make a knight and it's checkmate #shorts
PRKM.desc:
White to move: b8=Q, b8=R and b8=B all leave the black king on a6 without a move and not in check: stalemate. Only b8=N gives check, and with the bishop on b6 and the king on c6 it's checkmate.

Would you have made a queen?

#chess #underpromotion #chesspuzzle

NINQ.title: One side can have nine queens at the same time #shorts
NINQ.desc:
A pawn that reaches the last row can become a queen even if you still have your first one. Eight pawns can make eight new queens, so nine queens on one side is legal.

Did you know this?

#chess #chessrules #promotion

KNPM.title: This little pawn is the reason Black loses #shorts
KNPM.desc:
King and knight can never checkmate a bare king. But here Black's own pawn blocks a2, and 1.Nb3 is checkmate. Without the pawn the king would simply step to a2.

Did you know a knight can do this?

#chess #checkmate #chessendgame

CSB1.title: The rook crosses an attacked square, and castling is still legal #shorts
CSB1.desc:
When castling long, the rook passes b1, and it may be attacked. Only the king's squares count: e1, d1 and c1 must not be attacked. Here the bishop hits b1, and White can still castle.

Did you know this rule?

#chess #castling #chessrules
